recentItems.title: Syrian court sentences two to death over 2025 coastal massacres
recentItems.description:
A military court in the Syrian city of Aleppo has sentenced two people to death for their roles in mass killings in March last year. 
Two people were also acquitted in the trial while others were sentenced to prison for the killing of hundreds of civilians on Syria's west coast. 
The 10 defendants included loyalists to the former regime and members of the new government's security forces. 
It's the first time government-linked personnel have been put on trial for acts of violence. 

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett reports from Damascus, Syria.

recentItems.title: Ebola rumours in DRC are stopping people seeking treatment, WHO official says
recentItems.description:
Health authorities in Kenya have confirmed another case of Ebola just a week after the country recorded its first ever death from the virus.
The health ministry says the latest patient is a close family member of the first case.
He was already in quarantine when he developed symptoms and was immediately isolated.
The ministry says 108 people are in quarantine, but there's no evidence of wider community transmission.

Dr Catherine Smallwood is the World Health Organization's Incident Manager for the Ebola response in Democratic Republic of Congo. She says it's important that health officials take the rumours circulating around Ebola seriously so that they can combat them effectively.

recentItems.title: Ebola: A Virus Unleashed | The Full Report
recentItems.description:
An Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC is putting communities and health workers under renewed pressure in a region already struggling with conflict and displacement. The episode follows efforts to contain the virus, from identifying and treating patients to laboratory testing and safe burials, while examining how insecurity, mistrust and a fragile health system make the response more difficult.

recentItems.title: School roof collapse in Pakistan's Peshawar kills at least 29
recentItems.description:
A school roof has collapsed in Pakistan's Peshawar city, killing 29 people including students and teachers. 
Ambulances and rescue workers have rushed to the school where more than a dozen other people were also injured.
Other volunteers are helping to clear the rubble with buckets and baskets. 

Al Jazeera’s Kamal Hyder reports from Islamabad, Pakistan.
